id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979) and held posts at Ochanomizu University (~1981–1994) and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, later holding professorships at Bucharest (1934–1938), the Sorbonne (~1946–1948), and the University of Chicago (1957).

Mireille Bénisti worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying at École du Louvre and EPHE under Philippe Stern, Louis Renou, Jean Filliozat, and Paul Mus. She served at CNRS, Musées Nationaux, and taught at Phnom Penh and École du Louvre.
Mireille Helffer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a position as Chargé de Recherche at CNRS (~1964–1993) and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Mirella Keller is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned an MA from Fo Guang University (2015–2018) and a PhD from Eötvös Loránd University (2019), becoming an assistant professor at Dharma Gate Buddhist College in 2025.
Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. As attested in 2026, she holds posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Otago and the University of Calgary (PhD under John A. Baker) and held positions at the University of Western Australia and the University of New South Wales.

Miriam Levering worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at the universities of Zagreb and Ljubljana (PhD) and the International Faculty of Comparative Law. He held academic posts at Zagreb, Pennsylvania, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Yale University, including as Ford and Sterling Professor.
Miron Winslow worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Middlebury College (~1813–1815) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1815–1818), and later founded the American Madras Mission in 1836.

Miroslav Marcovich worked in Indology and philosophy. After studying at the University of Belgrade (~1937–1941), he held posts at Belgrade, Visva-Bharati, the University of Los Andes (1955–1959), and as Professor of Classics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1969–1989).
Mitashree Srivastava works in Buddhist studies. She completed an M.Sc at the University of Allahabad in 2007 and became an associate professor at the University of Delhi in 2013.
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied as a student under Ludo Rocher. He has held a post as professor at the University of Basel.

Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held an appointment in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 2009) and later served as professor emeritus there (attested 2026).

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies who studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1986–1991).
